title: api.paylane.io TLS certificate expired
alert: Synthetic check failed: https://api.paylane.io -> x509: certificate has expired or is not yet valid
logs: cert-manager: Certificate default/api-paylane-io is not Ready: Issuing certificate as Secret was previously issued by Issuer.cert-manager.io/letsencrypt-prod
cert-manager: Error presenting challenge: AccessDenied: User: arn:aws:sts::4421:assumed-role/cert-manager-irsa is not authorized to perform: route53:ChangeResourceRecordSets
root_cause: A Terraform IAM refactor dropped route53:ChangeResourceRecordSets from the cert-manager IRSA role, so DNS01 renewals had been silently failing for 30 days until the cert expired.
tried_failed: Deleting the Certificate secret (made it worse: ingress served the default fake cert)
fix: Restored the Route53 permission in terraform/iam/cert_manager.tf, then ran `cmctl renew api-paylane-io -n default`. New cert issued in ~2 minutes.

title: Checkout 5xx: Postgres connection slots exhausted
logs: psycopg2.OperationalError: FATAL: remaining connection slots are reserved for non-replication superuser connections
pgbouncer: closing because: no more connections allowed (max_client_conn)
root_cause: HPA scaled checkout-api to 16 pods; each pod opens a SQLAlchemy pool of 20 (DB_POOL_MAX=20), 320 client connections against pgbouncer max_client_conn=250.
tried_failed: Rolling restart of checkout-api pods (reconnect storm made it worse for ~5 min)
fix: Set DB_POOL_MAX=8 in the checkout-api ConfigMap and rolled the deployment. Errors cleared within 3 minutes.
follow_up: Size DB pools as max_client_conn / maxReplicas; documented in runbooks/checkout-db.md.

title: Notification backlog: poison message on notifications.v2
alert: Kafka consumer group notif-worker lag 92,000 on notifications.v2 and rising
logs: notif-worker: json.decoder.JSONDecodeError: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0) at partition=7 offset=18830211
kubelet: Back-off restarting failed container notif-worker
root_cause: A producer bug in merchant-portal wrote an empty payload to partition 7. The consumer crashed on it, restarted, re-read the same offset and crash-looped, stalling the whole group.
tried_failed: Restarting consumers (they re-read the same offset and crash again)
Scaling notif-worker to 12 replicas (no effect, partition 7 still blocked)
fix: Skipped the bad record: `kafka-consumer-groups --bootstrap-server kafka:9092 --group notif-worker --topic notifications.v2:7 --reset-offsets --to-offset 18830212 --execute` with consumers stopped. Lag drained in 11 minutes.
follow_up: Add a dead-letter topic notifications.v2.dlq and catch deserialization errors.

title: ledger-svc OOMKilled during nightly reconciliation
alert: ledger-svc pod OOMKilled (exit code 137) at 02:03 UTC, restart count 4
logs: recon: loading 1,840,112 transactions for 2026-07-29
kernel: Memory cgroup out of memory: Killed process 1 (python)
root_cause: The 02:00 UTC reconciliation job loads the entire previous day of transactions into memory; volume grew past what 2Gi can hold.
tried_failed: Raising the memory limit from 2Gi to 4Gi (it survived one night, then OOMed again the next day)
fix: Set RECON_BATCH_SIZE=5000 so reconciliation streams transactions in batches. Peak memory dropped to ~600Mi.
follow_up: RECON_BATCH_SIZE must be set in helm values for ledger-svc; unbounded load is the default.

title: Redis full: checkout session writes rejected
logs: redis.exceptions.ResponseError: OOM command not allowed when used memory > 'maxmemory'
root_cause: maxmemory-policy was noeviction and idempotency keys (idem:*) were written without a TTL, so memory filled up over three weeks.
tried_failed: FLUSHDB on the cache (dropped live checkout sessions, customers were logged out)
fix: `CONFIG SET maxmemory-policy allkeys-lru`, then backfilled a 24h TTL on idem:* keys with a SCAN script.
follow_up: Idempotency keys always get EX 86400. Never FLUSHDB the shared cache.

title: Postgres disk filling with WAL
logs: LOG: archive command failed with exit code 1
wal-g: AccessDenied: The AWS Access Key Id you provided does not exist in our records
root_cause: Quarterly credential rotation replaced the S3 key but not the wal-g secret, so WAL archiving failed and pg_wal could not be recycled.
fix: Updated the wal-g-credentials secret and restarted the archiver sidecar; archive backlog drained and disk fell to 54% in 40 minutes.
follow_up: Add wal-g secret to the credential rotation checklist; alert on pg_stat_archiver.failed_count.

title: Kafka broker disk at 95%
logs: kafka-log-dirs: audit.events size 1.4TB
root_cause: The audit.events topic was created with retention.ms=-1 (infinite).
fix: `kafka-configs --alter --entity-type topics --entity-name audit.events --add-config retention.ms=604800000`; audit data is also shipped to S3, so 7 days local is enough.
follow_up: Topic creation now goes through Terraform with required retention.

title: Payout batch started twice
alert: Two payout-scheduler jobs running concurrently for batch 2026-08-13
logs: payout-scheduler: starting batch 2026-08-13 (job payout-scheduler-29213460)
payout-scheduler: starting batch 2026-08-13 (job payout-scheduler-29213520)
root_cause: The CronJob had concurrencyPolicy: Allow and the batch ran longer than 1h, so the next schedule started a second run. The ledger idempotency check caught 97% of duplicates; 41 duplicate payouts had to be reversed.
fix: Suspended the CronJob, killed the second job, reversed duplicates via ledger-svc /admin/payouts/reverse. Set concurrencyPolicy: Forbid.
follow_up: Payout creation is idempotent on (payout_batch_id, merchant_id).

title: Stripe webhooks rejected in eu-west-1
alert: stripe webhook endpoint returning 400, 2.3k failed deliveries
logs: stripe.error.SignatureVerificationError: No signatures found matching the expected signature for payload
root_cause: The Stripe webhook signing secret was rotated but only updated in us-east-1; eu-west-1 still had the old STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET.
tried_failed: Rolling back checkout-api (no effect, it was config not code)
fix: Updated STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET in the eu-west-1 secret store and restarted; replayed failed events from the Stripe dashboard.
follow_up: Secrets are now synced across regions by external-secrets.

title: Checkout DB connection exhaustion during campaign traffic
logs: pgbouncer: no more connections allowed (max_client_conn)
sqlalchemy.exc.TimeoutError: QueuePool limit of size 8 overflow 0 reached
root_cause: A marketing campaign pushed HPA to 34 replicas; 34 x 8 = 272 connections, again over pgbouncer max_client_conn=250. Same pattern as INC-2104.
fix: Capped HPA maxReplicas at 28 and raised pgbouncer max_client_conn to 400 (default_pool_size unchanged). Recovered in 4 minutes.
follow_up: Check pool math whenever HPA limits change.

title: Intermittent DNS lookup failures
alert: Sporadic 'getaddrinfo EAI_AGAIN' and 'dial tcp: lookup ... i/o timeout' across services
logs: dial tcp: lookup ledger-svc.default.svc.cluster.local: i/o timeout
root_cause: conntrack race on UDP DNS in CoreDNS under load, amplified by ndots:5 (each lookup tried 5 search domains).
tried_failed: Scaling CoreDNS from 2 to 6 replicas (reduced, did not eliminate)
fix: Deployed NodeLocal DNSCache and set dnsConfig ndots:2 on high-traffic deployments.

title: All API logins failing after IdP key rotation
alert: auth-gateway 401 rate 100% for merchant API tokens
logs: auth-gateway: jwt validation failed: kid 'k-2026-08' not found in JWKS
root_cause: The identity provider rotated its signing key; auth-gateway caches JWKS for 24h and does not refetch on unknown kid.
fix: `curl -X POST http://auth-gateway:8081/admin/jwks/refresh` on every pod (or rolling restart). Recovered immediately.
follow_up: auth-gateway now refetches JWKS on unknown kid (rate-limited).

title: Payout files not delivered to partner bank
alert: payout-scheduler: 0 files delivered to bank SFTP in last 2h
logs: paramiko.ssh_exception.SSHException: Host key verification failed for sftp.northbank.example
root_cause: Partner bank rotated their SFTP host key without notice.
fix: Verified the new fingerprint with the bank by phone, updated the known_hosts ConfigMap, re-ran delivery.

title: Redis latency spike from KEYS *
logs: SLOWLOG: KEYS idem:* 1.9s client=10.2.14.7 (ops-admin-script)
root_cause: An ops admin script ran KEYS idem:* on the production cache, blocking the single-threaded server.
fix: `CLIENT KILL ADDR 10.2.14.7:*`, then added `rename-command KEYS ""` to the Redis config.

title: ledger-svc OOMKilled again at 02:00 UTC
alert: ledger-svc pod OOMKilled (exit code 137) at 02:04 UTC
logs: recon: loading 2,210,480 transactions for 2026-09-02
root_cause: The helm chart values refactor (PR #812) dropped RECON_BATCH_SIZE, so reconciliation went back to loading the whole day into memory. Regression of INC-2133.
tried_failed: Raising memory limit to 6Gi (on-call did this first before finding INC-2133; it still OOMed)
fix: Restored RECON_BATCH_SIZE=5000 in charts/ledger-svc/values.yaml and re-ran the job manually with `kubectl create job --from=cronjob/ledger-recon recon-manual`.
follow_up: ledger-svc now refuses to start reconciliation if RECON_BATCH_SIZE is unset.

title: Checkout outage after deploy v2.38: connections held across Stripe calls
alert: checkout-api 5xx 22%, p99 latency 7.4s, started 3 minutes after deploy v2.38
logs: sqlalchemy.exc.TimeoutError: QueuePool limit of size 8 overflow 0 reached, connection timed out, timeout 30
pgbouncer: no more connections allowed (max_client_conn)
root_cause: v2.38 moved the Stripe PaymentIntent call inside the DB transaction, so every checkout held a Postgres connection for the full Stripe round trip (~1.5s). Pool math was fine; hold time was the problem.
tried_failed: Raising DB_POOL_MAX to 16 (saturated pgbouncer faster, made it worse)
fix: Rolled back to v2.37 with `argocd app rollback checkout-api`. Errors cleared in 6 minutes.
follow_up: Lint rule: no outbound HTTP inside a DB session. If pool errors start right after a deploy, suspect connection hold time and roll back first.

title: notif-worker rebalance storm
alert: Kafka consumer group notif-worker lag 140,000 and rising
logs: notif-worker: Revoking previously assigned partitions
consumer poll timeout has expired. This means the time between subsequent calls to poll() was longer than the configured max.poll.interval.ms
root_cause: The SMS provider was slow (30s timeouts); a batch of 500 records exceeded max.poll.interval.ms=300000, so consumers were kicked from the group and the group rebalanced every few minutes. Not a poison message this time (DLQ was empty).
tried_failed: Skipping offsets like INC-2118 (wrong diagnosis, lost ~2k notifications that had to be replayed)
fix: Lowered SMS client timeout to 5s and max.poll.records to 50. Lag drained in 25 minutes.
follow_up: Check the DLQ and rebalance logs before resetting offsets.

title: Writes failing after Patroni failover
alert: checkout-api errors: cannot execute INSERT in a read-only transaction
logs: psycopg2.errors.ReadOnlySqlTransaction: cannot execute INSERT in a read-only transaction
patroni: promoted pg-1 to leader
root_cause: Patroni failed over to pg-1 after disk latency on pg-0, but pgbouncer was configured with pg-0's IP instead of the postgres-primary service DNS, so it kept sending writes to the now read-only replica.
tried_failed: Restarting checkout-api (pgbouncer still pointed at old primary)
fix: Pointed pgbouncer at postgres-primary.db.svc (the Patroni-managed endpoint) and ran `RELOAD` on the pgbouncer admin console.
follow_up: pgbouncer config is now generated from the service DNS, never IPs.

title: Ingress 502s after enabling trace baggage
logs: upstream sent too big header while reading response header from upstream
root_cause: New OpenTelemetry baggage headers pushed response headers over nginx's default 4k proxy buffer.
